failure: Knee Implant mechanical failure causing malfunction
constraint: Must maintain knee implant function within clinical specifications
mechanism: Mechanical dissociation at a modular implant interface due to failure of the locking mechanism, allowing disengagement while one component remains fixed in bone.
intervention: Add a secondary locking or anti-dissociation feature (e.g., a set screw or circumferential clamp) at the tibial insert-tray modular junction of the knee implant to prevent component separation while preserving normal articulation.
expected_effect: Maintains knee implant integrity under cyclic loading, prevents modular dissociation, and preserves function within clinical specifications.
falsification_test: Perform cyclic fatigue testing on knee implant constructs with and without the secondary locking feature; measure interface disengagement force after >10^6 cycles and compare to a clinical failure threshold.

source_evidence.source_title: Early Mechanical Dissociation of Helical Blade-Barrel Interface in Proximal Femoral Nail: A Case Report.
source_evidence.source_span: Introduction Proximal femoral nail (PFN) fixation is widely used for intertrochanteric (IT) fractures; however, implant-related complications remain a concern. While commonly reported failures include cut-out, back-out, and implant breakage, dissociation at the helical blade-barrel interface is extremely rare and poorly described in the literature. To the best of our knowledge, no prior case reports have described this specific mode of failure. Case report A 62-year-old male presented with pain
